faq_home_a1: Yes. The Free plan gives two hours of transcription per month, twenty AI summaries and eighty chat messages, with the full editor. No credit card. If you need more once, a 5-hour pack can be bought in one payment, no subscription. The code itself is free software, you can also host it yourself.
faq_home_a2: LinTO Studio Cloud is hosted in France by LINAGORA. Your files and transcripts are not used to train models and are not shared with third parties. For stricter needs, the same platform runs on your own infrastructure.
faq_home_a3: The 24 official languages of the European Union, for files and for live sessions, with simultaneous translation into several of them at once. Other languages are available on request.
faq_home_q4: Can LinTO join my Teams meetings?
faq_home_a4: Yes, from the Premium plan. A LinTO bot joins your Microsoft Teams, Jitsi, BigBlueButton and Visio (La Suite numérique) meetings, transcribes them live with participants' names, and the transcript lands in your workspace. Google Meet and Zoom are not supported yet.
faq_home_q5: I organize a conference. What do I need?
faq_home_a5: One audio feed per room, sent by your AV team like a YouTube live stream, and a screen or a QR code for the audience. We handle the rest, or we train your team to do it. See the live events page.

public_desc: Payment on invoice, dedicated hosting, installation on your servers, or a live setup for your conference: we send you a quote.
faq_p_a1: You are never billed per minute on your files, summaries or chat. On Premium, transcription stops at 30 hours in the month. Everything else, and all of Business, is unlimited within a fair-use policy defined in our terms of sale, which nobody reaches with normal work. If you do, the feature pauses until next month and we talk.
faq_p_a2: The unit for live transcription. One minute of live speech transcribed in its original language costs 1. Each live translation you switch on adds 1 per minute. A one-hour meeting transcribed and translated into two languages uses 180 language-minutes, that is 3 hours from your pack.
faq_p_q3: What counts as a seat in Business?
faq_p_a3: A seat is a member who can upload media or start a live transcription. Members who only read, comment or search are free. Usage is pooled across the team, however it is split between people.
faq_p_q4: Can I switch between monthly and yearly, or from Premium to Business?
faq_p_a4: Yes, from your organization's billing page. Changing plan is prorated. Changing period or cancelling is done in the billing portal and takes effect at the end of the current period.
faq_p_q5: What happens to my live minutes if I cancel?
faq_p_a5: Live packs are independent from the subscription. Minutes you bought stay valid 12 months after purchase, but using them requires an active Premium or Business plan.
faq_p_q6: I am a public body and cannot pay by card.
faq_p_a6: Contact us. LINAGORA issues an invoice on purchase order and activates your plan and live credits manually. Chorus Pro accepted.
faq_p_q7: Is the events mode included in Business?
faq_p_a7: No. Business covers your team's files, the meeting bots and the live microphone. Multiple rooms, AV feeds, scheduling and public pages belong to the live events offer, on quote. See the live events page.

faq_l_q1: What is the delay between speech and subtitles?
faq_l_a1: A few seconds. Text appears as the sentence is spoken and is finalized when it ends. Translations follow the finalized sentence, a few seconds later.
faq_l_q2: What does our AV provider need to do?
faq_l_a2: Send the audio of each room to an address we give them, exactly like a YouTube or Twitch live stream (SRT or RTMP). We test it together before the event. No hardware to rent.
faq_l_q3: Can attendees use it without an app?
faq_l_a3: Yes. The public page opens in any phone browser from a QR code or a link. It can be public, password-protected, or reserved to members of your organization.
faq_l_a4: No, it complements them: a written translation in rooms without an interpreter, and an accessible transcript everywhere. Wikimania 2026 had both: interpreters in some rooms, LinTO subtitles in all of them.
faq_l_q5: Can it run inside our own network?
faq_l_a5: Yes. The full stack, GPU models included, deploys on your Kubernetes or Docker infrastructure. Sensitive sessions never leave your site.
faq_l_q6: What do we keep after the event?
faq_l_a6: Every session becomes a transcript in your LinTO Studio workspace: editable, with speakers, exportable as DOCX, PDF, SRT or VTT, and summarized on request.

title_templates: Document templates for minutes and summaries - LinTO Studio guide
meta_description_templates: How to export LinTO Studio minutes and summaries in your own Word template: placeholders, upload, preview, DOCX and PDF export, API.
tpl_h1: Your own document templates for minutes and summaries
tpl_intro: LinTO Studio turns a transcript into minutes, a summary or a verbatim, then exports it. Out of the box you get DOCX, PDF, TXT and JSON. With a template, the export comes out in your own Word layout: logo, headings, fonts, footer. It takes about ten minutes to set up, and it works on every plan.
tpl_s1: 1. Start from a Word document you already use
tpl_s1_p: Take the file your team already fills by hand: the minutes template, the letterhead, the report skeleton. Keep its styles, header and footer. The template has to be a DOCX file under 10 MB.
tpl_s2_p: Write {{output}} where the AI text should land. It is the only required field. The generated content keeps its structure (headings, lists, paragraphs) and takes the styles of your document. A minimal template looks like this:
tpl_s2_p2: Other placeholders such as {{title}}, {{date}} or {{participants}} are optional. They are shown as a short form at export time so you can fill them in. On managed and on-premise deployments they can also be extracted from the transcript by the AI: ask us to configure an extraction prompt for your service.
tpl_s3_p: Open a transcript, generate a summary or minutes from the AI services menu, then click Publication and Upload a template. Give it a name and choose who sees it: only you, or your whole organization. On Business, a template uploaded for the organization is available to every member.
tpl_s4_p: Select the template and click Preview to check the result on the current document. Then export as DOCX to keep editing in Word, or as PDF for a final version. PDF is rendered server-side with LibreOffice, so stick to common fonts or embed them in the DOCX.
tpl_tip1: Make one template per document type: minutes, executive summary, verbatim. Each AI service can be linked to its own templates.
tpl_tip2: Keep tables and columns simple. The web preview does not render page breaks, text boxes or multi-column layouts; the PDF does.
tpl_tip3: A placeholder must stay in one run of text in Word. If Word splits {{output}} across formatting changes, retype it in one go.
tpl_tip4: Templates live with your organization. Rename, replace or delete them from the same Publication panel.
tpl_api_p: Everything above is available through the API with an API token: list templates, read their placeholders, export a document with a given template in DOCX, PDF or HTML. The document engine is the open-source LinTO LLM Gateway; its document templates guide covers extraction prompts and the export endpoints.
tpl_callout: Need a template designed to your charter, or extraction of specific fields (decisions, action items, deadlines)?

cm_eye2025_kicker: European Youth Event 2025 and 2026 · European Parliament, Strasbourg
cm_eye2025_title: 9,000 young people, 24 languages, one QR code
cm_eye2025_lead: On 13 and 14 June 2025, LinTO Live complemented the Parliament's interpreters: live transcription and translation in all 24 official EU languages, on attendees' phones. Back again in 2026.
cm_eye2025_p1: Around 9,000 young people from 160 nationalities, more than 450 debates, workshops and performances in the hemicycle and meeting rooms. Interpreters covered the main sessions; LinTO covered every room and added readable text to the interpreted ones.
cm_eye2025_p2: A QR code at the door of each room, one page per session, everyone in their own language, as subtitles or full transcript. More than 2,000 connections: attendees tuned in when the text helped them keep up, then went back to the room.
cm_eye2025_sv2: 95% found it easy or very easy to use, nobody answered “difficult”
cm_eye2025_sv3: 88% judged the subtitles early or very early
cm_eye2025_sv4: 85% found the captions understandable or mostly understandable
cm_eye2025_sv5: Deaf and hard-of-hearing attendees who do not use sign language reported overwhelmingly positive experiences
cm_eye2025_credit: Photo: © European Union 2025, source EP, Mathieu Cugnot

cm_wikimania_p2: A Wikimédia France volunteer built a multi-room dashboard on LinTO's API to check the state of every session at a glance. Its code is on Wikimedia's GitLab, like everything else.

cm_sofins2023_lead: SOFINS is the European meeting of special forces and their industrial partners. LinTO transcribed the inaugural address of Benoît de Saint Sernin live, as it was spoken.
cm_sofins2023_s2: new words added to the model
cm_sofins2023_p1: Military vocabulary is not in generic models. Before the show, the model was enriched with a 16-million-word catalogue of news and military documents: 53,000 new words.
cm_sofins2023_p2: During the speech, the text is displayed as it is spoken and contextual errors are corrected retroactively every three words. Under 1% error at the end.

cm_posais2026_kicker: Paris Open Source AI Summit, 2nd edition · Maison de la Radio et de la Musique, Paris · 10 July 2026
cm_posais2026_title: The open-source AI summit, subtitled from the Studio 104 control room
cm_posais2026_lead: A day of talks in French and English in an 800-seat hall, co-organised by LINAGORA and OpenLLM France. LinTO transcribed and translated the sessions live, and Benjamin Bellamy showed it on stage.
cm_posais2026_p1: Studio 104 of the Maison de la Radio: a control room, the stage audio feed, a laptop. The text comes out in French and English for an audience from all over Europe.
cm_posais2026_p2: At 9:45, LinTO demo on stage. The Affiches Parisiennes noted a first demo “a bit shaky” with the hazards of live, which “still revealed the effectiveness of this open AI tool”.
cm_posais2026_alt1: The LinTO operator in the Studio 104 control room during the summit
cm_prs2026_kicker: Paris Radio Show 2026 · La Bellevilloise, Paris · 3–4 February 2026
cm_prs2026_title: A booth, a microphone, a transcript running in front of the radio industry
cm_prs2026_lead: The trade show of radio, audio and podcast professionals: around 7,000 visitors and a hundred exhibitors every year. First time for LINAGORA, with LinTO demonstrated non-stop.
cm_prs2026_p1: A microphone behind a reflection filter, a laptop, a QR code: visitors speak, the text appears, they scan and find the transcript on their phone.
cm_prs2026_p2: Benjamin Bellamy and Gaël Lago held the booth for two days. For a radio station the point is simple: every programme becomes text that is accessible, translatable and searchable, without sending the audio outside Europe.
cm_prs2026_alt1: The LinTO booth at Paris Radio Show: microphone, laptop and QR code poster
cm_wikimania_alt5: Laptop and audio interface set up in a room at Wikimania 2026
pf_free_pack_small: one-time payment, no subscription, valid 12 months
pf_premium_transcription: 30 hours of file transcription per month
faq_p_q8: I only have one big file to transcribe, do I need a subscription?
faq_p_a8: No. The Free plan can buy a 5-hour pack for €10, in one payment. The hours add to the 2 monthly hours and stay valid for 12 months.
